subject: Renewal: Pinebrook Systems — usage floor, price shelf, and roll-forward options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pinebrook.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@pinebrook.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal and optional roll-forward for Pinebrook Systems

Hi Emma / Jordan —

Thanks again for the thoughtful renewal convo last week. Per our discussion, attached is a clean outline of a renewal approach that balances Pinebrook's need for rate stability with some flexibility on committed capacity. High level: 

- 12-month price shelf: lock current committed rates for 12 months from renewal effective date.
- Usage floor on new commit: 70% utilization of committed units (i.e., 30% allowed slippage) before true-up.
- Roll-forward credits: allow unused committed units to roll forward up to 6 months, capped at 25% of the annual committed amount.
- One-time onboarding credit: $50,000 applied to month 1 invoice for signature within 30 days.

I attached our usage history (Q1–Q2) and a PDF with the proposed term language ("Proposed_renewal_term_v3.pdf"). If this is directionally acceptable, can we lock a 30-minute call next week to finalize commercials and timing? We'd like to close by end of June to guarantee capacity slot for Q3.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Pinebrook_Usage_History_Q1-Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Proposed_renewal_term_v3.pdf (summary of commercial terms)

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pinebrook.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@pinebrook.com>, procurement@pinebrook.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and optional roll-forward for Pinebrook Systems

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the history file. A couple of things coming back from procurement and finance: 

1) The one-time credit is helpful but we need a slightly better effective headline rate to stay within our FY28 budget.
2) Procurement is pushing for roll-forward at 50% of the annual commit (rather than 25%) since our usage tends to be seasonal; they want the ability to move more headroom to Q3/Q4.
3) If you can extend the price shelf to 18 months, that would make the internal ask easier.

Jordan is on copy to coordinate the procurement timeline — we are hoping to get a signed amendment to hit July invoices. Can you share a counter with those levers considered? Also include any constraints from your side if we ask for a larger roll-forward.

Thanks,
Emma Liu
VP, Platform Ops | Pinebrook Systems
emma.liu@pinebrook.com

--
Jordan Hayes
Director, Procurement | Pinebrook Systems
jordan.hayes@pinebrook.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal proposal and optional roll-forward for Pinebrook Systems

Team — forwarding Pinebrook's asks (see below). Immediate items we need to decide: extend price shelf to 18 months? increase roll-forward cap to 50%? deepen or keep onboarding credit? Procurement wants a lower effective rate.

My read: they value price stability more than deeper discounts, but procurement will push hard on roll-forward. Operational concerns: higher roll-forward increases our capacity planning uncertainty (we could be retaining spare capacity longer). Suggested counter (initial thoughts):

- Price shelf: keep 12 months firm; offer an optional 6-month extension (to 18 months) if they convert to a 24-month commit (i.e., multi-year incentive).
- Roll-forward: increase to 35% cap (from 25%), with roll-forward allowed only once per quarter and must be used within 6 months.
- One-time credit: keep $50k, but make it contingent on signature within 30 days.
- If they need a lower headline rate, offer a stepped discount tied to firmed commit: e.g., 10% discount at 100% annual commit vs. 7% at 80% commit.

Markus — can you comment on risk/ticketing for 35% roll-forward and whether we need a max outstanding roll-forward cap (absolute $/units)? Lauren — ops implications and whether the "once-per-quarter" rule is practical. Aditya — any flexibility on the onboarding credit or alternative commercial levers (credits vs. extended billing term)?

Vanessa

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal proposal and optional roll-forward for Pinebrook Systems

Vanessa — quick notes:

- Capacity risk: 35% roll-forward is workable but we should cap outstanding roll-forward exposure at 40% of annual commit in $ terms to avoid large month-to-month spikes.
- Operational guardrails: require roll-forward requests 10 business days before the start of the quarter and automatic conversion of rolled units to billed usage if not consumed within 6 months.
- Legal/billing: add a clause that any rolled units beyond the cap convert to overage billing at the agreed overage rate.

I like the multi-year swap for an 18-month shelf (gives predictability).

Markus

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pinebrook.com>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@pinebrook.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal and optional roll-forward for Pinebrook Systems

Emma / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear asks — we've taken internal alignment and can propose the following counter (summary + attached updated term PDF):

Counter (commercial highlights):
- Price shelf: 12 months guaranteed at current committed rates. Optional extension to 18 months if Pinebrook signs a 24-month committed term (multi-year).
- Roll-forward: up to 35% of annual committed units may be rolled forward, usable within 6 months. Roll-forward must be requested 10 business days before quarter start; rolls may be submitted once per quarter.
- Outstanding roll-forward cap: absolute cap of 40% of annual commit (in units/$) to limit exposure.
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice if signed within 30 days.
- Stepped discount: 10% effective discount at 100% annual commit; 7% at 80% commit.
- Overage: any consumption beyond rolled/committed units billed at published overage rates (see attached).

We think this preserves the price stability you want while keeping our capacity planning manageable. If you need a firmer 18-month shelf without a multi-year commitment, we can discuss a smaller additional fee to guarantee capacity — happy to outline that option.

If this looks good, can we aim to have a final sign-off by Wednesday, June 30 to lock the Q3 slot? I've attached the updated term sheet (Proposed_renewal_term_v3.pdf) and a clean one-pager.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: Proposed_renewal_term_v3.pdf (updated counter), OnePager_Pinebrook_Renewal.pdf

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@pinebrook.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@pinebrook.com>, procurement@pinebrook.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Pinebrook Systems — usage floor, price shelf, and roll-forward options

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for carving out the middle ground. Pinebrook is comfortable moving forward with your counter in principle:

- We accept the 12-month shelf with the multi-year pathway to 18 months.
- Roll-forward at 35% (with the 40% outstanding cap) is acceptable given the 6-month use window.
- We will proceed with the $50k onboarding credit contingent on signature within 30 days.

Legal needs to run the updated term sheet; Jordan will coordinate the DocuSign. Expect procurement to route the amendment by EOD Monday. Please send the final redline-ready DocuSign packet to procurement@pinebrook.com and cc me.

Appreciate the responsiveness — excited to keep scaling together.

Best regards,
Emma Liu
VP, Platform Ops | Pinebrook Systems
emma.liu@pinebrook.com

Procurement note: Jordan will send the required PO number and vendor paperwork with the DocuSign envelope.
